summary: Expose one loaded-Document boundary for the Markdown Share collaborative workspace.
context: App.tsx mixed routing and Document loading with presence, editor sync, pane, viewport, scroll, display, checkpoint, and rendering behavior. The implementation needed better locality without expanding the selected architecture candidate.

options.label: Move the complete collaborative workspace behind one loaded-Document component
Extract many small hooks and rendering components
options.rejectedBecause: This would create shallow interfaces and distribute tightly coupled browser mechanics.

options.label: Also extract checkpoint history as a vertical slice
options.rejectedBecause: That is a separate architecture candidate and would expand scope beyond the selected refactor.

choice: Move presence, sync, editor, pane, viewport, scroll, display, checkpoint, and rendering behavior into one collaborative workspace module that accepts a loaded public Document.
rationale: The page layer now depends on one domain-shaped capability, while tightly coupled workspace details remain local and private. This reduces App.tsx from 1364 to 201 lines without inventing general abstractions.
consequences: The collaborative workspace module remains intentionally large because it owns one cohesive runtime.
Checkpoint history stays internal until its separate vertical-slice refactor is explicitly selected.
Behavioral tests can render the workspace directly without routing or Document-query setup.

evidence.excerpt: App.tsx now contains 201 lines and delegates a loaded Document to CollaborativeWorkspace.
Typecheck, lint, 43 tests, production build, and real-browser interaction checks pass.
